title: Graded lane orchestrator with consumption-feedback and elastic spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a graded-lane orchestrator that enforces tier-aware routing (free / paid / enterprise) while making admission decisions from live quota consumption signals and region affinity. The orchestrator should: 1) consult per-tenant quota state and short-term consumption rate to compute admission probability and lane assignment; 2) prefer regional replicas with lower egress latency when tenant region affinity exists; 3) pick graceful fallback model variants (quantized/light model, lower-context variant) when preferred model capacity is unavailable or quota signals indicate degradation; 4) emit per-request routing diagnostics to Console for traceback and cost attribution.

Scope and non-goals: scope includes admission logic, policy evaluation, metrics, rollout knobs, and end-to-end tests. Non-goal: major runtime kernel changes or introducing new model formats. We will rely on existing model-variant registry and runtime compat layers.

High-level design: the orchestrator sits in the routing plane and runs a two-stage decision: (A) Eligibility filter — is a request admissible for preferred lane given quotaBudget, recent consumptionRate, and SLO tags; (B) Selection stage — choose region-capable endpoint and model variant. Eligibility uses an exponential-decay window of consumption (configurable half-life) and a configurable buffer credit. When quota is low, requests may be demoted to a lower-cost lane or served with a smaller model variant. For enterprise tenants with reserved capacity, route to reserved pools and bypass demotion logic except under extreme overload and explicit fallback rules.

Policy config: JSON schema will include: allowed_lanes (ordered), soft_threshold_pct, hard_threshold_pct, decay_half_life_secs, reserve_burst_tokens, regional_affinity_weight, fallback_priority_list (list of model variant ids), emergency_fallback_region_set. Defaults are safe for free tier (aggressive demotion) and permissive for enterprise.

Observability & metrics: emit per-decision tags: routed_lane, selected_model_variant, admitted (true/false), quota_before, quota_after, regional_choice, admission_reason. Add dashboard: Lane Utilization, Demotion Ratio by plan, Median latency by lane, Failover frequency by region. Include tracing span in request path for debug.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated (ff:graded_lane_orchestrator). Canary on internal/dev tenants -> beta customers (paid) -> enterprise with opt-in. Monitor demotion rate and error budget impact. Provide an override API for support.

Testing: unit tests for eligibility math and policy parsing, integration tests against mock quota service and runtime endpoints, load test scenarios simulating bursts (20x normal) and regional outage to verify graceful spillover.

Migration: default policy is a no-op that mirrors current behavior until flag enabled. Backwards-compatible with existing per-tenant quota store. Admins can set per-tenant policy overrides via Console.
comments: 2025-01-09 - Aisha Patel: Initial spec drafted and shared to #infra-smart-routing. Key open questions: decay half-life default, interaction with caching layer, and how to represent enterprise reserved bypass rules in config.

2025-01-15 - Tomás García (review): Suggested moving regional_affinity_weight into a per-tenant override and exposing it in Console. Raised concern about tight coupling with KV cache invalidation during demotion; recommended adding a cache-tag in tracing output. Action: Maya to add cache-tag and update tests.

2025-01-22 - Maya Chen: Prototype eligibility evaluator implemented. Local benchmarks show decision latency adds ~0.35ms p50 on cold path and ~0.08ms p50 on warm path. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/712. Load tests in staging indicate demotion reduces peak tokens by ~42% for free-tier burst shapes.

2025-01-30 - Design (Liam O'Connor): Reviewed UX for Console policy editor. Requested explicit textual warnings for configurations that may cause aggressive enterprise demotion. Linked spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SR/Graded+Lane+Orchestrator+Spec

2025-02-04 - Reliability (Nina Li): Ran chaos test simulating eu-west outage. Behavior: spillover to us-east triggered and 98% of requests remained served with quantized_small model. Observability gap found: per-request region_choice missing for some cached responses. Ticket created: ENG-37801 (cache-region-tagging).

2025-02-10 - Maya Chen: Opted to add a short-lived soft-reserve buffer (reserve_burst_tokens) to reduce false-positive demotions during brief spikes. Default set to 200 tokens for free tier after empirical tuning. Updated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/733

2025-02-12 - PM (Evan Brooks): Approved canary plan for paid accounts starting 2025-02-20. Metrics to watch: demotion_rate <= 3% for paid, latency regression <= 5% p95. Set release target: runtime-1.20.
Open blocker: finalize SLA override semantics for enterprise. Security note: ensure audit logs record any demotion decision for enterprise tenants. Security review requested.

Follow-ups: 1) wire Console policy editor to policy schema; 2) add end-to-end test that asserts correct model-variant fallback under regional failure; 3) coordinate with billing to ensure cost attribution tags are present for demoted requests.
